title: Questionnaire Evidence Automation: Adapter Patterns & SIEM Mapping
content:
Purpose
This working doc proposes a set of adapter patterns and mappings to automate customer security questionnaire responses using audit-log artifacts and RBAC v2 metadata, and to produce SIEM-friendly exports for evidence review. Target audience: security engineers, solutions engineers, and product owners responding to customer questionnaires or building trust center artifacts.

Scope and goals
- Reduce manual effort for recurring questionnaire items by making evidence discoverable and machine-queryable.
- Provide a set of adapter patterns (push/pull/hybrid) for integrating Redwood audit logs, RBAC v2 state, and supporting artifacts with customer-facing questionnaire responses.
- Define a compact audit-log -> SIEM mapping (JSON + CEF examples) tuned for most customer assessments.
- Recommend evidence naming and packaging conventions to tie logs to questionnaire questions and Confluence/Jira artifacts.

High-level flow patterns
1) Pull Adapter (recommended for ad-hoc questionnaire runs)
   - Security responder executes an evidence collection job that queries the internal audit-log datastore (timebox), RBAC state store, and config repo.
   - Adapter composes: short answer text + links to artifacts + a small manifest that references log slices (start/end, query id, hash).
   - Use cases: customer security questionnaire, SOC 2 evidence requests, offline audits.

2) Push Adapter (recommended for ongoing continuous assurance)
   - Periodic exporter runs in infra and pushes pre-bundled, QA’ed evidence packages into a secure evidence bucket (s3) and notifies a ticketing system.
   - Each package includes: manifest.json, sampled log excerpts, RBAC snapshot, KMS key reference, and summary.md.
   - Use cases: managed customers with frequent audits, partner integrations that prefer push notifications.

3) Hybrid Adapter (best for semi-automated customer responses)
   - For each questionnaire, an automation runner fetches available pre-bundles and combines with on-demand queries for missing pieces.
   - Provides fastest time-to-response while preserving freshness for critical items.

RBAC v2 considerations for questionnaire answers
- When a question asks "Who can view audit logs?" we should provide: short answer, RBAC role names, role-to-permission mapping, last time role membership changed, and an example log entry showing an access event.
- Export a sanitized RBAC snapshot: role list, permissions (namespaced), user/service principal count, assigned resources. Provide a hash and timestamp to prove snapshot immutability.
- For least-privilege evidence: produce a role-explain artifact that shows which roles grant a given permission (reverse mapping). This supports 'principle of least privilege' claims.

Audit log schema (recommended core fields)
- timestamp: ISO8601
- event_id: UUID
- principal_type: user | service | anonymous
- principal_id: stable id (prefer hashed email for customer exports)
- action: canonical string (e.g., model.generate, key.rotate, admin.role.assign)
- resource_type: e.g., model, deployment, key, route
- resource_id: opaque id or path
- result: success | failure | denied
- reason: optional free text (authorization failure details)
- request_metadata: { ip, agent, region } (see privacy notes below)
- trace_id: correlates with request traces for incident reconstruction
- retention_label: audit | operational | pii

Notes: customer-facing artifacts should redact PII per policy and include only the minimum fields necessary to support the claim. For SIEM exports we map these fields to the SIEM schema (examples below).

SIEM export mapping patterns
- JSON (preferred for modern SIEMs): export each log entry as a single JSON object with the core fields above. Attach a "evidence_reference" field that links to the bundle manifest or Confluence page.
- CEF/LEEF (required for some partners): map `event_id`->extension ID, `timestamp`->startTime, `principal_id`->duser, `action`->cs1Label/cs1. Use a consistent mapping table maintained in the exporter.
- Minimal enrichment: add `rbac_snapshot_hash`, `questionnaire_id` (if the export was produced for a request), and `export_bundle_id`.

Example JSON export (single entry)
{
  "timestamp": "2024-10-15T09:12:23Z",
  "event_id": "7a1b2c3d-...",
  "principal_type": "service",
  "principal_id": "svc-abc123",
  "action": "admin.role.assign",
  "resource_type": "role",
  "resource_id": "role-readonly-logs",
  "result": "success",
  "trace_id": "trace-xyz",
  "evidence_reference": "s3://redwood-evidence-bundles/evidence-20241015-0001/manifest.json"
}

Evidence manifest conventions
- manifest.json fields (flat): bundle_id, created_at, created_by, hash, scope_hint (e.g., tenant or org), questionnaire_ids (list), artifacts (list of artifact filenames), rbacsnapshot_id, retention_policy.
- Filenames should follow: <bundle_id>/<artifact_type>-<short>-<YYYYMMDD>.ext (e.g., evidence-0001/rbac-snapshot-20241015.json).
- Manifests must include a succinct human-readable summary.md with the one-line answers to questionnaire items and pointers to log slices.

Sample Q&A snippets (for reuse in responses)
Q: Who can access production model tokens/logs?
A (short): Access to production model logs and token material is limited to a small group of operations principals and an automated rotation service; access is recorded in the audit log and accessible via our SIEM export. See manifest s3://.../evidence-20241015-0001 for RBAC snapshot and sampled log entries.
Q: How do you prove role changes are authorized?
A (pattern): Provide the RBAC change log slice + the approval ticket id (Jira) and a signed manifest hash. The change log entry includes actor, timestamp, and related approval artifact link.

Redaction and privacy rules
- Customer-facing bundles must redact or pseudonymize personal data by default. Use stable pseudonyms (hashes with a per-bundle salt) and preserve referential integrity within the bundle.
- IP address removal: either drop IPs or replace with /24 masked CIDR for region-level evidence.
- Keep a private sanitized mapping table internally so we can re-associate if an internal incident needs investigation (but do not include the mapping in customer bundles).

Developer notes: exporter components
- Collector: reads event store (time-range or query id), applies retention and redaction policy, emits canonical JSON.
- Enrichment: attaches rbac_snapshot_hash, ticket links, and manifest pointers.
- Packager: bundles artifacts into an encrypted s3 path and writes manifest.json.
- Notifier: creates a ticket with bundle link and posts to Slack channel used by the responder/external CA.

Open questions / decisions to make
- Should we maintain a "questionnaire taxonomy" index so automated runners can map questions to queries? (recommended yes; light-weight taxonomy required).
- Export auth model: do we grant customers temporary secure presigned URLs to evidence bundles or do we deliver via a dedicated SCP/partner exchange?
- Sampling policy for logs: how large a slice do we include as representative evidence? Propose default 1 hour + sampling heuristics for noisy endpoints.

Next steps / immediate action items
- (SEC-412) Build a prototype Pull Adapter that accepts a questionnaire_id and returns: short answers.md, manifest.json, and 5 sampled log entries. Owner: Owen. ETA: 3 weeks.
- Update RBAC v2 snapshot API to expose role-explain endpoint. Owner: Kai. ETA: 2 weeks.
- Define taxonomy for top-30 questionnaire items and map to queries. Owner: Maya + CS. ETA: 4 weeks.

Appendix: quick references
- Confluence: RBAC v2 design notes (linked).
- Jira: SEC-412 (automation prototype).
- Implementation hint: the exporter should support both JSON newline-delimited exports and CEF/LEEF for legacy partners.

Notes to reviewers
This is an early draft. Focus feedback on: (a) evidence manifest fields we must include for legal/compliance, (b) preferred SIEM formats we must support, and (c) redaction defaults.
